license_message: Sign in inside the RONE Plugins Center to unlock your plugins. Bought or claimed a plugin but never set a password? Sign in with that e-mail and we will send you the link to set one. New here? Free trial at roneaudio.com.

center_installer.whats_new: 2.1.25: Learn gets a Start Here row with the install videos, the trial reads 14 days everywhere, and RONE 1176 and 2A stand in My Rack with their hardware. 2.1.24: a cleaner tray menu, in the RONE look. 2.1.23: RONE VST MANAGER on the Library banner - every plugin you own in one library, with Install and its full video guide. 2.1.22: updating RONE VST MANAGER no longer asks you to close it - the Center closes it, updates it and opens it again by itself (Windows). 2.1.21: the Center opens with its logo drawing itself - the R writes its line in purple light, then the library opens (Windows). 2.1.20: the light on the new-drop banner sweeps across the unit in one smooth loop. 2.1.19: RONE Control's LINK works again on Windows 11 with the new Windows MIDI system - the "RONE Control" MIDI port now comes from Windows itself, so FL Studio, Live and REAPER hear it with no restart and no extra driver. 2.1.18: RONE VST MANAGER has its own place in the sidebar - one click opens it (or installs it first). 2.1.17: RONE VST MANAGER also reaches ALL ACCESS members and everyone who unlocked it with a story. 2.1.16: a gift for every RONE customer who bought a plugin or ALL ACCESS - RONE VST MANAGER, every plug-in on your computer in one library with pictures, loaded onto your track in one click. Install it from the card at the top of the Library. 2.1.14: a calmer, brighter Library - white is the Center's colour, each plugin card glows in its own neon with its 3D unit faintly at its edge, the new-drop banner turns its unit slowly in the light, and plugin and Center updates share one bar. The preview player is gone. 2.1.12: the Center wears the RONE PLUGINS colours - white on graphite - and each plugin keeps its own. 2.1.11: updates reach Windows as soon as they are ready, and on a Mac each update shows its own version. 2.1.10: RONE Sidechain arrives with its own icon and its 3D unit. 2.1.9: your plugins stay unlocked even if our licence server has a hiccup, and if a computer ever needs you to sign in again to keep them unlocked, the Center says so. 2.1.8: behind the scenes, the Center tells us which RONE versions this computer runs - so when an update matters (like the new INFINITE bars in Flanger) we make sure it reaches you. 2.1.7: the RONE Analyzer card wears its new cyan icon. 2.1.6: an update that waits for a program to close now says exactly which one - including FL Studio's own plug-in hosts (ilbridge.exe and the scanner) - and when one of those is left running after FL Studio itself has closed, the Center ends it and installs. 2.1.5: your own prices - right after a purchase, one plugin picked for it at $19 for a day (its tutorial plays muted until you tap the speaker); an owner price on every RONE plugin you don't have yet; a first plugin offer for a free account; and a Settings switch to hear about deals first. 2.1.3 (Mac): Settings > Updates without a password. One button moves your RONE plugins from the system folders into your own (one last password), and from then on every update installs with no password. 2.1.2: when an install fails, the Center now says why - and how to fix it - instead of 'installer code 0'. 2.1.1 (Mac): a plugin whose user folder (~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3 or Components) the Center may not write to - often made by another company's installer - now installs system-wide with your password instead of failing with 'Permission denied'.

plugins.name: RONE Reverse Reverb
plugins.description: Tempo-synced reverse reverb for risers, vocal swells and seamless transitions - tail lengths from 1/32 to 8 bars, shaped with fades, filters and stereo width
plugins.whats_new: 1.2.10 - FIX: the plugin window no longer goes black or white for a moment when another window overlaps it, for example with two plugins open. It stays on screen now, and it opens on the dark background instead of white. 1.2.9 - FIX: the plugin window no longer goes black when the mouse is over it. Yesterday's update hid the page whenever another window seemed to sit on top, and it took the plugin's own file-drop layer for one (Live, Studio One) - now only a real window in front counts. 1.2.8 - With the plugin window minimised, closed or behind another window (in FL Studio, the mixer), the place where it sat no longer catches the mouse: the DAW's own buttons and faders there can be clicked again. 1.2.7 - the knobs and the popover lists now work on older Macs too (macOS before Big Sur): on those Macs the page could stop loading and the lists did not open. 1.2.6 - the RONE look is now one across the line: the knob of Reverse Reverb / Flanger with the value inside it, keys without the grey frame, selectors that glide, lists that open as a RONE popover instead of the system list, and the glow only where you touch. The tremolo lists open as popovers. 1.2.5 - On Windows the mouse wheel now works inside the plugin: lists and menus scroll, and controls that take the wheel turn with it. 1.2.4 - When two windows of the plugin open together (two instances in one project), the second no longer stays white. The plugin carries its own fonts, so it looks the same with no internet connection, and the small labels are larger and easier to read. 1.2.3 - In Ableton Live the plugin now fills its window: with Auto-Scale Plug-In Window on and a screen scaled above 100 %, the interface no longer sits in a corner with a white band, and it refits when you move it to a monitor with a different scale. 1.2.2 - LIVE now catches every take: press LIVE again after the phrase (or stop the song) and the riser is made from what the channel just played. A stop that heard nothing says so on the screen instead of doing nothing.

pt.description: Reverb reverso sincronizado ao tempo para risers, swells de voz e transições sem emenda - caudas de 1/32 a 8 compassos, moldadas com fades, filtros e largura estéreo

es.description: Reverb inverso sincronizado al tempo para risers, swells de voz y transiciones sin cortes - colas de 1/32 a 8 compases, moldeadas con fades, filtros y anchura estéreo

plugins.name: RONE Stutter
plugins.description: Tempo-locked stutter engine - beat divisions, sculpted fade curves and stereo movement for instant fills, edits and glitch builds
plugins.whats_new: 2.0.3 - On ORIGINAL, picking a transient (a click, PREV or NEXT) now plays it at once, up to the next transient, with no trip to PLAY. FIX: the plugin window no longer goes black or white for a moment when another window overlaps it, for example with two plugins open. It stays on screen now, and it opens on the dark background instead of white. 2.0.2 - FIX for Cubase: dragging the RESULT into the project works again. Cubase put the plugin window over the layer that catches the drag, so pressing on the waveform and pulling did nothing (EXPORT still worked). 2.0.1 - FIXES from a user in FL Studio: clicking the waveform on ORIGINAL, or pressing PREV / NEXT, no longer throws you over to RESULT - pick your start point in peace (STUTTER still shows the result). PREV / NEXT now step from wherever your point is, not only from a transient. NEW: drag the right edge of the CHUNK on ORIGINAL to set its length - it snaps to the grid (1/2 to 1/32), or sets the ms on FREE. Dragging the RESULT into the DAW works even when you press, wait a moment and then pull. On Windows, opening another plugin window over Stutter no longer turns it black or makes it flicker, and that window gets its own clicks again. 2.0.0 - LIVE: Stutter now works in real time, on the channel itself. A big EDIT / LIVE switch sits beside the logo. EDIT is the Stutter you know: drop a file, shape the fill, drag it out. LIVE stutters whatever plays through the channel, with no latency, and it sounds exactly like the fill you built in EDIT - every preset, GRID, RAMP, COMPLEX row, KEY, filter and fade. AUTO (the default): play the song and the fills come by themselves, on its bars - one every 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars, BARS long, at the END of the phrase (landing on the next downbeat) or at its START. With BARS as long as EVERY it never stops. HOLD and ONE-SHOT play it by hand: the HOLD pad, the six macro slots as pads (an empty slot plays a ready sound), MIDI notes C3 to F3 for pads 1 to 6 and any other note for the panel (VST3 - route a MIDI track to Stutter), or the Live Trigger parameter as automation. CATCH lands a press on the next 1/16, beat or bar, so it is always in time. When the song stops, LIVE lets go. In the AU version the pads take no MIDI; the pads on screen and the automation work. 1.7.4 - FIX: the plugin window no longer goes black when the mouse is over it. Yesterday's update hid the page whenever another window seemed to sit on top, and it took the plugin's own file-drop layer for one (Live, Studio One) - now only a real window in front counts. 1.7.3 - COMPLEX sounds like the sample again: after a SLOW or RISE step, the steps that followed came out slightly dull, as if a low-pass were on (up to -6 dB at 15 kHz). PLAY, ROLL and STUCK now play the source exactly, and pitched slices and the tape steps keep their top end too - in COMPLEX and in the GRID. Filters and fades stay where you set them, in ADVANCED and EXTRAS. 1.7.2 - With the plugin window minimised, closed or behind another window (in FL Studio, the mixer), the place where it sat no longer catches the mouse: the DAW's own buttons and faders there can be clicked again. 1.7.1 - PLAY LOCK: the new padlock key next to RESULT keeps the preview playing in a loop, so you can flip through presets and hear each one at once - every change starts the loop again from the top (on the next bar with ON BAR while the song plays). DICE is now a die, and the COMPLEX steps get their own row, so the FADE IN knob no longer covers them. 1.7.0 - COMPLEX: a new key at the end of the GRID row turns the fill into a row of steps, like FL's Chop > Complex. Each step is ROLL (with its own grid), STUCK, PLAY, SLOW, RISE (tape stop and spin-up), REV or GAP, and can carry its own pitch. FOLLOW reads on through the sample, HOLD restarts every step, HITS cuts on the transients. Click a step to edit, split, join, copy or delete it; DICE rolls a new row. 40 new presets: COMPLEX CATCHES, TAPE, GLITCH, BUILDS and PSYCHEDELIC, TREMOLO GATES and more PSYCHEDELIC. FADE OUT and STEREO AUTO now have a RANGE: drag the handle at the end of the ring to set where the sweep ends. 1.6.9 - the knobs and the popover lists now work on older Macs too (macOS before Big Sur): on those Macs the page could stop loading and the lists did not open. 1.6.8 - STEREO now works on mono samples (most one-shots are mono): the fill comes out in stereo and the hits jump left and right as they should. Before, STEREO did nothing on a mono file. 1.6.7 - the RONE look is now one across the line: the knob of Reverse Reverb / Flanger with the value inside it, keys without the grey frame, selectors that glide, lists that open as a RONE popover instead of the system list, and the glow only where you touch. FADE OUT and STEREO are real arc knobs with their AUTO under them. 1.6.6 - On Windows the mouse wheel now works inside the plugin: the preset list scrolls, and knobs and values turn with the wheel. 1.6.5 - When two windows of the plugin open together (two instances in one project), the second no longer stays white. The plugin carries its own fonts, so it looks the same with no internet connection, and the small labels are larger and easier to read. 1.6.4 - EXTRAS now opens above the RESULT button, so you can tweak and hear the result without closing it. 1.6.3 - FILTER RANGE: with HIGH PASS / LOW PASS AUTO on, drag the handle at the end of the ring to set where the sweep stops (the readout shows the range, e.g. 100 > 2.0k). Double-click it to go back to the full sweep. 1.6.2 - FILTER AUTO: HIGH PASS and LOW PASS can now sweep across the fill, like FADE OUT and STEREO AUTO - the knob is where it starts, UP / DOWN sweep it to the end. A new FILTER LIN / EXP switch in EXTRAS shapes the sweep. 1.6.1 - In Ableton Live the plugin now fills its window: with Auto-Scale Plug-In Window on and a screen scaled above 100 %, the interface no longer sits in a corner with a white band, and it refits when you move it to a monitor with a different scale. 1.6.0 - FILTER: a HIGH PASS and a LOW PASS in EXTRAS, baked into the rendered fill (24 dB/oct, all the way to the end = off). Saved with the project and the presets. Double-click on PITCH now resets it to 0.

pt.description: Motor de stutter travado no tempo - divisões de batida, curvas de fade esculpidas e movimento estéreo para fills, edits e builds glitch na hora

es.description: Motor de stutter fijado al tempo - divisiones de pulso, curvas de fade esculpidas y movimiento estéreo para fills, edits y builds glitch al instante

plugins.description: One knob that grabs the loop and rolls it up - the captured slice shrinks tighter and tighter until it screams, then lets go right back into the beat

plugins.name: RONE Clipper
plugins.description: FREE plugin - sign in to the Center with a free RONE account and it unlocks. A hard clipper that shows you exactly what it cut: the waveform after the clip stage with the removed peaks in blue, one CLIP knob, LOW CUT that keeps kick and bass out of the clipper, and integer-latency oversampling that nulls against the input at -100 dB

plugins.name: RONE Rise
plugins.description: One knob, the whole build-up: turn INTENSITY up over the phrase and the mix becomes a rise (a steep high-pass, a big reverb, echoes, noise, a barber-pole climb), snap it to zero and the drop hits with the reverb still spilling into it - or press GO and let it land on the bar by itself
plugins.whats_new: 1.0.16 - FIX: the plugin window no longer goes black or white for a moment when another window overlaps it, for example with two plugins open. It stays on screen now, and it opens on the dark background instead of white. 1.0.15 - PRESETS: a preset bar on top with 17 new factory presets (PSY GATE, TRANCE BUILD, SUBMARINE, WARP DRIVE, CHAOS and more). SAVE keeps your macros as your own preset, or as the macros of a mode card - saved on your computer for every project; the gear brings back the factory macros. TAIL is now CUT by default, with a quick CUT / 1-4 bar switch next to BYPASS. KILL LOW reaches 3 kHz at 100 % in every mode (your existing projects sound exactly the same). The five modes have new names: LIFTOFF, ORBIT, PULSAR, UNDERTOW, MELTDOWN.

pt.description: Um knob, o build-up inteiro: suba o INTENSITY ao longo da frase e a mix vira um rise (high-pass íngreme, reverb grande, ecos, ruído, uma subida infinita), zere no drop e o reverb ainda transborda nele - ou aperte GO e deixe pousar no compasso sozinho

es.description: Un knob, todo el build-up: sube INTENSITY a lo largo de la frase y la mezcla se vuelve un rise (high-pass pronunciado, gran reverb, ecos, ruido, una subida infinita), llévalo a cero en el drop y la reverb aún se derrama en él - o pulsa GO y deja que aterrice en el compás solo

plugins.name: RONE Flanger
plugins.description: A transition riser flanger - sweep it by hand or engage INFINITE barberpole mode for endless bar-locked rises and falls, with feedback, stereo offset and a rhythmic gate
plugins.whats_new: 2.1.10 - RONE Flanger now works on mono tracks too: mono, and mono in with stereo out, where STEREO still adds width. In Logic it shows up on mono channel strips as well. Stereo tracks sound exactly as before. 2.1.9 - Mac: RONE Flanger now also comes as an Audio Unit, so it opens in Logic Pro and GarageBand. Update it from the RONE Plugins Center and rescan your plugins if it does not show up at once. 2.1.8 - FIX: the plugin window no longer goes black or white for a moment when another window overlaps it, for example with two plugins open. It stays on screen now, and it opens on the dark background instead of white. 2.1.7 - FIX: the plugin window no longer goes black when the mouse is over it. Yesterday's update hid the page whenever another window seemed to sit on top, and it took the invisible overlays of NVIDIA, Discord, Steam or the Xbox Game Bar for one - now only a real window in front counts. 2.1.6 - With the plugin window minimised, closed or behind another window (in FL Studio, the mixer), the place where it sat no longer catches the mouse: the DAW's own buttons and faders there can be clicked again. 2.1.5 - the knobs and the popover lists now work on older Macs too (macOS before Big Sur): on those Macs the page could stop loading and the lists did not open. 2.1.4 - the RONE look is now one across the line: the knob of Reverse Reverb / Flanger with the value inside it, keys without the grey frame, selectors that glide, lists that open as a RONE popover instead of the system list, and the glow only where you touch. INFINITE and GATE are switches. 2.1.3 - The plugin carries its own fonts, so it looks the same with no internet connection, and text you need to read is never the faint grey. 2.1.2 - In Ableton Live the plugin now fills its window: with Auto-Scale Plug-In Window on and a screen scaled above 100 %, the interface no longer sits in a corner with a white band, and it refits when you move it to a monitor with a different scale. 2.1.1 - AUTO GAIN keeps working in hosts that send empty audio blocks, at high FEEDBACK the ring now stops when you stop the song while bounces keep the real tail, a user preset saved under a factory preset's name now loads, and the Windows standalone has an AUDIO button for audio and MIDI settings. 2.1.0 - INFINITE starts its sweep from the same point every time you switch it on - by hand, by automation, or when you press play with it already on - instead of wherever the song happened to be in the cycle, which could start a riser in the middle or at the end. Automate INFINITE on the bar where the rise should begin and it climbs the same way every time; the start lands on the nearest 1/16, so automation drawn on the bar line starts exactly there. A loop that jumps back before that point starts the sweep again. 2.0.9 - On older Macs (Safari before 14.1) the window's controls now sit where they belong: labels inside their knobs, rows spaced, nothing in a corner. 2.0.8 - INFINITE has three new lengths: 32 BAR and 16 BAR for long builds, 1/4 (one beat) for a fast shimmer - eight in all, from 32 bars down to a quarter bar. Projects and presets saved with an older version open on the length they had; only automation drawn on the sweep length in an older project needs redrawing. 2.0.7 - FIX: OUTPUT works while you play. Turning it, or automating it, now changes the level at once (with a 20 ms ramp) instead of only after the audio restarted. GATE no longer clicks: the effect fades in and out over 5 ms right on the grid line, where it used to switch hard on the edge of the audio buffer (up to a whole buffer late), and the flanger keeps running while the gate is closed, so every pulse comes back clean. 2.0.6 - UPDATE NOTICE: when a newer version is out, the plugin says so as it opens. UPDATE hands it to the Plugins Center, which installs it as soon as your DAW lets go of the plugin (closing the DAW always does); until then the plugin is grey and your settings stay as they are. LATER hides the note for three days. 2.0.5 - the mouse wheel moves every knob (shift = fine); the About panel's texts are readable. Host automation now moves the knobs. The interface follows the plugin's own parameters live, so an automation clip, a host preset recall or a second open window all show up on screen instead of leaving the controls frozen where you last left them. Every move you make is also wrapped in an automation gesture now, so hosts in Touch or Latch record it properly.

plugins.whats_new: 1.3.54 - FIX: the correlation meter no longer lets the quiet tail of a sound outweigh its hit. A clap or a snare with a wide tail could read negative while the sound as a whole sits safely positive; the reading now follows where the energy is. 1.3.53 - FIX: the plugin window no longer goes black or white for a moment when another window overlaps it, for example with two plugins open. It stays on screen now, and it opens on the dark background instead of white. 1.3.49 - Internal tidy-up: no change to the sound, the measurements or the screen. 1.3.48 - FIX: the plugin window no longer goes black when the mouse is over it. Yesterday's update hid the page whenever another window seemed to sit on top, and it took the invisible overlays of NVIDIA, Discord, Steam or the Xbox Game Bar for one - now only a real window in front counts. 1.3.47 - With the plugin window minimised, closed or behind another window (in FL Studio, the mixer), the place where it sat no longer catches the mouse: the DAW's own buttons and faders there can be clicked again. 1.3.46 - The meters, the spectrum and the vectorscopes draw again on older Macs (macOS before Big Sur), where 1.3.43-1.3.45 showed no graphs while the buttons still worked. 1.3.45 - The second vectorscope has its own CORRELATION meter and stands the same size as the first, so the two read side by side. 1.3.44 - The reference now shows its own level: muting a channel in your track no longer moves the reference bars or the FULL wave. SOLO BAND and MONO now work on the reference too, so you hear it filtered like your mix. MIX is a chip in the CHANNELS row - drag it to choose who is drawn in front. A + on the vectorscope opens a second vectorscope beside it, showing the loaded reference or any Channel in its own colour (update the RONE Analyzer Channel with the app). 1.3.43 - the RONE look is now one across the line: the knob of Reverse Reverb / Flanger with the value inside it, keys without the grey frame, selectors that glide, lists that open as a RONE popover instead of the system list, and the glow only where you touch. The app carries the RONE fonts (Sora, Manrope, IBM Plex Mono). 1.3.42 - In Ableton Live the plugin now fills its window: with Auto-Scale Plug-In Window on and a screen scaled above 100 %, the interface no longer sits in a corner with a white band, and it refits when you move it to a monitor with a different scale. 1.3.41 - However many channels you put in, every channel chip is reachable: the chips shrink to fit, and past that the CHANNELS row scrolls sideways when you roll the wheel over it, with a fade on the side that has more. 1.3.40 - BAR SCOPE: roll the mouse wheel over the scope to stretch the wave taller, up to 16 times, to see exactly where the kick hands over to the bass; the HEIGHT chip shows how far and puts it back. A beat looped in your DAW under 1/4 BAR no longer draws the bass (or the kick) with a doubled outline - each pass now replaces the last. To reorder the channel chips, hold one: it lifts, the others wobble and make room, and it settles where you drop it. The NOTE pop-out button sits under the word NOTE, and SCOPE has moved to the bottom right of the vectorscope. 1.3.39 - NOTE pops out: the small button at the end of the NOTE row opens the note in a little window of its own that stays on top of everything - put it over your EQ, in front of your eyes. Drag it anywhere; its X and grip show when the mouse is on it. A MIX chip in the CHANNELS row hides the master on the spectrogram, so you see only your channels. Drag the channel chips left and right to choose which one is drawn on top - the one on the right. 1.3.38 - The update notice and the menus are in the Analyzer's cyan, like its icon. 1.3.37 - The SIDES chip on the spectrogram turns off again with a second click, and the vectorscope on SIDES no longer paints the side spectrum over the bars. 1.3.36 - The BAR SCOPE keeps a RONE Analyzer Channel's wave whole: in FL Studio it kept wiping itself, so only a sliver of the bar - one bass note - stayed on screen. 1.3.35 - The BAR SCOPE draws your RONE Analyzer Channels on the bar, each in its own colour - a Channel on the kick and one on the bass show as two waves over the master. A new chip picks MIX + CH, CHANNELS alone or MIX alone, and the channel chips over the spectrogram pick which channels; with only the channels it works without the Bridge. A channel on the spectrogram now moves as fast as the master. A band solo shades the same distance either side of the point you hold. The vectorscope chip goes STEREO, SIDES, MONO: SIDES shows only the side signal, and with the Bridge your DAW plays it. Reopen your DAW project once after this update so it loads the new Channel and Bridge. 1.3.34 - A new icon in the RONE cyan with a thin wave, the same mark as the header. The level meter's 0 dB row is red, the line nothing should cross. The stray MON caption under the spectrum is gone. 1.3.33 - RONE Analyzer Channel: a small plugin for any mixer channel - name it KICK, BASS, VOX, pick its colour - and the analyzer draws that channel's spectrum over the master's, in its colour, exactly as the master is drawn (LED columns in BARS, the FFT curve in WAVES), up to eight channels. A CHANNELS row over the spectrogram: click a chip to show or hide it, S to see it alone, right-click to hear it alone through the Bridge. The Bridge and the Channel share one new face in the RONE cyan. 1.3.31 - FIXED keeps the spectrogram and the level meter one shape with the bar scope open or closed and with the chrome hidden: the window follows instead of stretching them. The level meter has two red OVR rows over 0 dB and yellow rows from -3 dB up, fills its height, and the peak bar settles before it falls. The rules are a step fainter. The frequencies sit right under the plot, the zone names under them. The Bridge becomes the source the moment it appears in the DAW, and a Bridge loaded before an update keeps working until the DAW reloads it. The reference in WAVES is measured with the same FFT as the live curve. A new default theme, RONE. 1.3.30 - HINT: a tour of everything (Menu > Hints, or F1), a step per control with a short animation of the gesture. Ten new themes, each with its own RMS, peak and SIDES colours: Graphite, Ice, Phosphor, Ember, Fjord, Tokyo, Mocha, Rose, Solar, Mono. The level meter has ten LEDs between one number and the next, as the classic hardware has it. The bar scope stays live while you zoom and draws the zoom from the samples. Loading a reference no longer runs the analyser over the record; only the reference strip shows the progress. The right-click browser menu is gone. 1.3.29 - RULES chip on the spectrogram: a click hides the 5 dB rows, the next hides the 10 dB rows too, the next brings them all back. In BARS every zone (SUB, BASS, LOW MID...) is whole bars, its border in the gap between two bars, and a zone solo shades whole bars. A held peak is a whole LED in the peak colour, on the analyser and on the level meter. The menu's highlight stays inside the menu. 1.3.28 - The yellow rules sit on the numbered rows: a level's row is the LED lit when the signal reaches it, the number sits on it and the rule takes it, in the spectrum and in the level meter. The 5 dB marks are LED rows too, fainter. The level meter's rules stay inside each column. Every menu now hangs from the chip that opened it, flush with its edge, with one soft shadow. 1.3.27 - DAW / REF: with a reference loaded on the RONE Bridge, a round switch where PLAY was flips between your track and the reference - the DAW is muted while the reference plays and the meters show it (reopen the Bridge in your DAW once after this update). REF FULL works in WAVES too, as a spectrum in the reference colour. The 10 dB rules are LED rows now, as in the classic hardware, lit with the bar and dim over the dark LEDs; the LEDs fill the plot to the top; the menus and the Setup lists are drawn in the house look. 1.3.26 - Lighter on the computer: the same picture for less than half the work. The meters draw at about 60 frames a second on any screen (a 144 Hz monitor used to get 144), the LED bars and peak caps are drawn once and reused, and when nothing is playing the panels rest until something moves. 1.3.25 - The yellow 10 dB rules and the fainter 5 dB lines are back over the Spectrogram's bars, and with them the reference lines, the live average and the readout under the pointer - 1.3.23 had stopped drawing them in BARS. 1.3.24 - Settings live on their panels, the way the classic hardware lays them out: the spectrogram's gear opens the Spectrum Analyser settings, a new gear on the level meters opens the Level Meter settings, and the vectorscope's gear the Goniometer settings (in WAVES the spectrogram's gear is the FFT's own settings). the FFT's Routing - Stereo, Mid, Side, Left, Right - is in WAVES' settings. A large Block Size no longer leaves the WAVES curve standing still: it moves at least 24 times a second, with the same levels. The analyser and the level meters stand on whole screen pixels like the classic: every LED the same size at any window size, the plot growing a whole LED at a time as the window is resized. MAX PEAK and MAX RMS are readings now, not buttons. 1.3.23 - In WAVES the spectrogram's gear opens the FFT's own settings: Type, Window, Block Size, Overlap, Avg Time, a second spectrum, Filled display, Anti-alias, Align 0 dB, Offset, Smooth, Freq and Range limits and Slope, with the FFT's choices and a DEFAULT that brings back the FFT's factory mode - so whoever comes from the FFT analyser sets it the way they know (in BARS the gear is the classic Setup, as before). The vectorscope draws like a beam: threads of light that are bright where the signal moves slowly and faint where it jumps, with a soft glow. A right click on a zone name under the spectrum solos that zone alone; right click it again for the whole mix. 1.3.22 - Stability: the RONE Analyzer Bridge lets go of its fonts safely when a DAW unloads it (FL Studio could crash on exit after its window had been open), ignores empty audio blocks, and turns a NaN coming from a plug-in before it into silence instead of passing it on. A DAW that changes its sample rate no longer reconfigures the Analyzer from its audio thread. On a Mac the source is no longer closed and opened again by one passing licence check, which made macOS ask for permission again (the repeated Allow prompts). 1.3.21 - WAVES is now the familiar FFT analysers as the FFT analyser opens: the same FFT (2048, Hann, 50 % overlap), the same 2-second average, the same 4.5 dB per octave slope and the FFT's own scale, -78 to -18 dB with its numbers, so a frequency reads in WAVES what it reads in the FFT analyser. In Ableton Live the BAR SCOPE lines up on the kick: Live gives every plug-in the same song position whatever latency sits before it (a limiter, a linear-phase EQ), so the picture ran late; the scope now measures that from the kick and slides the picture back, and says by how much. The BAR SCOPE opens with HOLD off. FIXED size now sits on whole screen pixels instead of between them, so it draws sharper. On a Mac, listening to what the Mac plays through a multichannel interface reads that interface's own output pair at its real level, and an interface with many inputs no longer hides the capture. 1.3.20 - The zones under the spectrum - SUB, BASS, LOW MID, MID, HIGH MID, PRESENCE, AIR - are buttons now: click one and only that range plays through the RONE Analyzer Bridge, click more to add them, click a lit one to take it out, Escape for the whole mix again. MAX PEAK and MAX RMS show the live figure, the highest of the last two seconds, so there is no RESET to press. The vectorscope is sharp again: Release is the time a dot takes to fade, the dots are single pixels, and the diamond fills its panel. REF FULL draws the reference in the same column as your mix: above it where the record is louder, as a line inside it where your mix is. 1.3.19 - WAVES now reads what the bars read: every point is the power in a third of an octave, with the bars' own release, so a frequency shows the same dB in both views (the FFT's per-bin levels and 4.5 dB slope sat 15 dB under the bars). The maximum is a thin line over the curve instead of a second filled body. 1.3.18 - NOTE: the note under the mix - the fundamental of the bass or the kick - reads under the reference strip, with its octave, hertz and cents. The Spectrogram has a BARS / WAVES switch (W): WAVES draws an FFT spectrum the way the FFT analyser draws one - the real-time average filled, the real-time maximum behind it, the FFT's 4.5 dB per octave slope - so anyone used to the FFT analyser reads it at once; the bars are exactly what they were. The frequency zones - SUB, BASS, LOW MID, MID, HIGH MID, PRESENCE, AIR - are named along the bottom of the plot. Reference curves can be saved by name and brought back later without loading the record again (REFERENCE, or CURVES under the strip), and REF LINE / FULL draws the reference as a line over the bars or as bars of its own beside them. While a record is being read the strip shows its progress, and says so in red when a file cannot be read. The header is cleaner: SOURCE holds the channel pairs, and FILE, RESET and SETUP live in the menu. 1.3.17 - The vectorscope is back to its classic dot picture. On a Mac, choosing a sound card as the source opens it once instead of twice, so macOS has fewer reasons to ask for permission again. 1.3.16 - The reference plays: PLAY under the strip plays its 16 bars round and round on your computer's output (stop your DAW to compare), and CLEAR takes the record away. The strip now opens on the loop where every band is lit - the drop with the hats and percussion in - rather than wherever the kick and bass are loudest. 1.3.15 - REFERENCE has a strip of its own under the correlation meter: load a record and its waveform comes up with the tempo found for you; the curve on the Spectrogram is taken from a loop of 16 bars - it opens on the loudest one, the arrows move it 16 bars at a time and a click puts it anywhere, so you compare against the part with every layer in. The vectorscope draws the signal as a glowing trace with a soft cloud around it. Appearance > Customize sets the SIDES colour. The overs are two red clip lamps. The bar scope stays on the sum. On a Mac the title bar no longer shows a title that sat off to one side. 1.3.14 - MAX PEAK and MAX RMS now sit at the top of the LEVEL METERS, read exactly the way StandardCLIP reads them - the largest sample, and the RMS averaged over 217 ms, louder channel - so a kick shows the same numbers in both; click either to reset them. SIDES on the Spectrogram paints the side signal over the bars in violet: what is wide, band by band. Fainter lines at every 5 dB (Appearance > Spectrum 5 dB lines hides them). In the BAR SCOPE, a slide off the grid now shows as an amber OFFSET chip - click it to put the kicks back on the beat. On older Macs the bar scope and the level meters draw whole again (they showed only the tips of each kick, or nothing). The correlation meter's white tick is gone. 1.3.13 - The meters keep drawing on older Macs, a second Analyzer Bridge no longer scrambles the readings, the window always opens on screen, and if the Analyzer ever crashes the report reaches us through the Plugins Center.

tips.text: Draw the Stucker knob up exactly on the hit you want caught: it grabs what starts where the knob comes up, every time.

i18n.pt: Desenhe o knob do Stucker subindo exatamente no hit que você quer capturar: ele pega o que começa onde o knob sobe, sempre.
i18n.es: Dibuja el knob de Stucker subiendo justo en el golpe que quieres atrapar: atrapa lo que empieza donde sube el knob, siempre.

tips.text: Turn Rise up over the last 8 bars and snap it to zero on the drop: the reverb still spills into the first hit.

i18n.pt: Suba o Rise nos últimos 8 compassos e zere no drop: o reverb ainda transborda no primeiro hit.
i18n.es: Sube Rise en los últimos 8 compases y llévalo a cero en el drop: la reverb aún se derrama en el primer golpe.

tips.text: Turn LOW CUT up so the kick and bass stay out of the clipper, then push CLIP until the blue only touches the transients.

i18n.pt: Suba o LOW CUT para o kick e o baixo ficarem fora do clipper, depois empurre o CLIP até o azul só tocar os transientes.
i18n.es: Sube LOW CUT para que el kick y el bajo queden fuera del clipper, luego empuja CLIP hasta que el azul solo toque los transitorios.

tips.text: Put Reverse Reverb on the last word before the drop: the swell runs straight into the hit, with no gap.

i18n.pt: Coloque o Reverse Reverb na última palavra antes do drop: o swell entra direto no hit, sem buraco.
i18n.es: Pon Reverse Reverb en la última palabra antes del drop: el swell entra directo en el golpe, sin hueco.

tips.text: INFINITE at 32 BAR gives a rise that never stops climbing: automate MIX up over the build.

i18n.pt: O INFINITE em 32 BAR dá um rise que nunca para de subir: automatize o MIX ao longo do build.
i18n.es: INFINITE en 32 BAR da un rise que nunca deja de subir: automatiza MIX a lo largo del build.
